blocks.orig: The costs for a Tanzania visa differ slightly per nationality. Are you from Europe? Then the fee is 50 USD. Are you a US citizen? blocks.orig: All foreigners visiting the country need to get this insurance, regardless of your own travel insurance. With this, the Tanzania government aims to protect travellers who come to Tanzania and reduce the financial risk for the Tanzanian government.
blocks.html: Every foreign visitor must take out this insurance, whatever travel insurance you already have. The Tanzanian government’s aim is to protect visitors to Tanzania and to lower its own financial risk.

blocks.orig: The basic coverage of this mandatory travel insurance includes the cost of emergency medical expenses, repatriation expenses, baggage loss, and emergency evacuation. The costs of the insurance are 44 USD per person, and it’s valid for 92 days (multi-entry). Children of 17 years or younger pay 22 USD, while infants up to 2 years don’t need to pay. To apply for Tanzania’s mandatory travel insurance online, please visit the website of the National Insurance Corporation. After payment, you receive a QR code to be shown upon arrival. Alternatively, you can obtain this insurance upon arrival in the country at all land border crossings and at the international airports, including Kilimanjaro International Airport (JRO) and Julius Nyerere International Airport (DAR).

blocks.orig: Passport: This is a no-brainer, but it can sometimes be tough to remember to pick up your passport on your way out of the door. Make a note about remembering your passport somewhere that you can be sure that you will see it, such as on the fridge or on the bathroom mirror. Also, make sure that your passport has a minimum validity of six months.

blocks.orig: Tanzania experiences both wet and dry seasons, with the dry seasons falling between January and February and then between June and October and the wet seasons lasting from March to May and then from November to early December.

blocks.orig: For a safari in the dry season, you aren’t likely to see any rain, but it’s best to pack a few jackets just to be sure. Otherwise, light clothing will suffice. The wet seasons call for heavier clothes, such as scarves and thicker jackets.

blocks.orig: Tanzania weather differs from region to region – but there is always a great time to travel in Tanzania! Weather in the coastal areas is the hottest and most humid, while the North and highlands of Tanzania are cooler because of altitude. The temperatures vary between 22 °C and 31 °C throughout the year. During the night, the temperature in Tanzania drops to between 10 °C and 22 °C. The beaches of Zanzibar have a distinctively tropical climate, since it is located close to the Equator. On this page, you can read more about the weather in Tanzania.

blocks.orig: Plan to wear layers so you can acclimatize to weather variations. Instead of dark blue or black, which tends to draw tsetse flies, wear neutral or khaki-coloured clothing so that you blend right in. Sunglasses, insect repellent, sunscreen, and wide-brimmed hats are essential. blocks.orig: You’re probably curious about the country you’ll soon be exploring. To help you get acquainted, we’ve gathered a few useful facts about Tanzania. From its currency and official languages to time zone and population – here’s everything you need to know before your adventure begins.
blocks.html: You are likely curious about the country you’ll soon be discovering. To help you get to know it, we have put together some handy facts about Tanzania. From the currency and official languages to the time zone and population – here is what you should know before your adventure starts.

blocks.orig: The local currency is the Tanzanian shilling. And even though dollars and euros are still used in the most touristic places, the only official currency is the Tanzanian shilling and should be used, especially for all your small expenses.
blocks.html: Tanzania’s local currency is the Tanzanian shilling. Dollars and euros are still accepted in the most touristy places, but the Tanzanian shilling is the only official currency and the one to use, particularly for small purchases.

blocks.orig: There are over 100 different languages spoken in Tanzania. The official languages, however, are Swahili and English. You can expect all your Your Tanzania Trip guides and hosts to speak English, but if you’re looking to learn a few words of Swahili before your trip, check out our list of top 25 useful words in Swahili!
blocks.html: More than 100 languages are spoken in Tanzania, but Swahili and English are the official ones. All your Your Tanzania Trip guides and hosts will speak English, but if you would like to pick up some Swahili before you travel, have a look at our top 25 handy Swahili words!

blocks.orig: Swahili is spoken by almost everyone. In the tourism sector, however, English is widely spoken by the majority of people.
blocks.html: Almost everyone speaks Swahili. In the tourism sector, however, the majority of people speak English well.

blocks.orig: The population of Tanzania is almost 60 million. One of Africa’s most ethnically diverse countries, around 125 different ethnic groups live in Tanzania, with more than 100 different languages spoken nationwide.
blocks.html: Tanzania has a population of almost 60 million. It is one of Africa’s most ethnically diverse countries, home to roughly 125 ethnic groups, and more than 100 languages are spoken across the nation.

blocks.orig: The Tanzanian people are well-known for their hospitality, often warmly welcoming tourists to experience their beautiful nature, wildlife and culture. If you really want to learn more about the country and its culture, be open and talk to the locals.
blocks.html: Tanzanians are known for their hospitality and often give visitors a warm welcome to their beautiful nature, wildlife and culture. To really get to know the country and its culture, be open and chat with local people.

Traditional Tanzanian food

Traditional Tanzanian food

blocks.orig:
Traditional Zanzibar food

Here’s a guide to help you decide the best time for your Tanzanian adventure. Oh, and before we forget… everyone is different, which is why there is no correct choice. blocks.html: When to visit Tanzania depends on what you would like to see, where you want to travel, your budget and your interests. Every season has advantages and drawbacks. This guide will help you choose the right time for your Tanzania adventure. And before we forget… everyone is different, so there is no single right answer. blocks.orig: Below you can find some answers to frequently asked questions. For more detailed information, check out our article “When is the Best Time To Visit Tanzania?”
blocks.html: Below are answers to some frequently asked questions. For more detail, read our article “When is the best time to visit Tanzania?”

blocks.orig:
June to October & December to February
These months are the crème de la crème for visiting Tanzania! That’s why we rated them “Excellent”. Think of June to October as nature’s blockbuster season: sunny skies, wildlife galore, and the epic Great Wildebeest Migration. December to February is like hitting the safari jackpot, with lush green landscapes and adorable baby animals everywhere.
blocks.html:
June to October & December to February
These are the very best months to visit Tanzania, which is why we rate them “Excellent”. June to October is nature’s headline season: sunshine, plenty of wildlife and the epic Great Wildebeest Migration. December to February is a real safari treat, with lush green scenery and adorable young animals all around.

blocks.orig: But hey, March, April, May, and November are also cool to go – especially if you love vibrant greenery, bird-watching, and having the park almost to yourself. Yes, there might be some rain, but not all the time and it’s still a great time to visit Tanzania.
blocks.html: That said, March, April, May and November are good months too – particularly if you love vivid greenery, birdwatching and having the park almost to yourself. Some rain is possible, but not constantly, and it remains a great time to travel to Tanzania.

blocks.orig: Great news: You can witness the awe-inspiring Great Wildebeest Migration all year long as it moves between the Maasai Mara in Kenya and the Serengeti in Tanzania. No matter when you travel, you won’t miss this incredible event. Here’s a breakdown about when and where you can see the highlights, so you can choose what’s most important to you!
blocks.html: Good news: the impressive Great Wildebeest Migration can be seen all year round as it moves between Kenya’s Maasai Mara and Tanzania’s Serengeti. Whenever you travel, you won’t miss this remarkable spectacle. Here you’ll find an overview of when and where to see the highlights, so you can decide what matters most to you!

blocks.orig: Tanzania’s weather varies by region, but there’s always a great time to visit! The coastal areas are the hottest and most humid, while the northern regions and highlands are cooler due to their higher altitude. Temperatures generally range from 22 °C to 31 °C during the day, dropping to between 10 °C and 22 °C at night. Zanzibar’s beaches enjoy a distinctly tropical climate thanks to their proximity to the Equator.
blocks.html: The weather in Tanzania differs by region, yet there is always a good time to go! The coast is the hottest and most humid, while the north and the highlands are cooler because they lie higher. Daytime temperatures usually range from 22 °C to 31 °C, falling to between 10 °C and 22 °C at night. Being close to the Equator, Zanzibar’s beaches have a clearly tropical climate.

blocks.orig: Tanzania has two seasons per year: the wet and the dry season. The wet season (also called the rainy season) runs from the end of October right through to December, and then again from the end of March to the beginning of June. They are referred to as “short rains” and “long rains”. These tropical rains mostly start late afternoon and continue all night till early morning. The rains of Africa are famous worldwide and are a soothing, enchanting sight to behold during a trip to Tanzania!
blocks.html: Tanzania has two seasons a year: the wet season and the dry season. The wet (or rainy) season lasts from the end of October all the way to December, and again from the end of March to early June. These periods are known as the “short rains” and the “long rains”. The tropical showers usually begin in the late afternoon and carry on through the night until early morning. Africa’s rains are famous around the world, and watching them on a trip to Tanzania is a calming, magical experience!

blocks.orig: Absolutely. In fact, National Geographic, Discovery and other major media companies choose the rainy season on purpose to shoot their wildlife documentaries in Tanzania. The weather is fantastic all year round and even though heavy rains persist most afternoons in the rainy season, the natural environment comes to life. Nature is colourful, the grass is lush and green, beautiful flowers grow, animals find plenty of food, temperatures are nice and cool and, better yet, the main highlights of Tanzania are far less crowded with tourists.
blocks.html: Certainly. National Geographic, Discovery and other large media companies even pick the rainy season deliberately to film their wildlife documentaries in Tanzania. The weather is excellent all year, and although heavy rain falls most afternoons in the rainy season, the landscape comes alive. Nature turns colourful, the grass is lush and green, lovely flowers bloom, animals have plenty to eat, temperatures stay pleasantly cool and, best of all, Tanzania’s main highlights see far fewer tourists.

blocks.orig: Another benefit of travelling in rainy season is the lower costs of safaris and accommodation. The disadvantages? Some accommodations are closed, and sometimes the roads are in a poor condition. Fortunately, this mainly concerns the roads in the national parks in South Tanzania.
blocks.html: A further advantage of a rainy-season trip is that safaris and accommodation cost less. The downsides? Some accommodations close, and roads can be in bad shape. Luckily, this applies mostly to the roads in the national parks of South Tanzania.

blocks.orig: For those travelling to Tanzania during the rainy season, the following national parks are open and ready for your visit: Serengeti, Ngorongoro Crater, Tarangire, Lake Manyara, Lake Natron and Arusha National Park.
blocks.html: If you travel to Tanzania in the rainy season, these national parks are open and ready to welcome you: Serengeti, Ngorongoro Crater, Tarangire, Lake Manyara, Lake Natron and Arusha National Park.

blocks.orig: During the wet season, some national parks are better to avoid, such as Nyerere, Ruaha, Mikumi and Udzungwa. So if any of the latter destinations are on your must-do list in Tanzania, you’d better head out during the dry season.
blocks.html: Some national parks are best skipped in the wet season, including Nyerere, Ruaha, Mikumi and Udzungwa. If any of these are high on your list for Tanzania, it is better to go in the dry season.

blocks.orig: The rain turns the landscape green, which attracts a lot of animals. This means plenty of opportunities to spot wildlife at their finest – and happiest! During the rainy seasons, animals are more active, which makes for a fantastic safari experience. With an abundance of food and fresh water, animals roam in their thousands. The rain also protects the animals from the harsh heat of the sun.
blocks.html: Rain turns the scenery green, and that draws in many animals. You get lots of chances to see wildlife at its best – and at its happiest! Animals are more active in the rainy seasons, which makes for a superb safari. With food and fresh water everywhere, they roam in their thousands. blocks.orig: Tanzania yellow fever requirements can sometimes seem confusing, but we’re here to help! As a yellow fever-free country, Tanzania is safe to travel when it comes to steering clear of this virus. You may have more questions about it, so let’s answer them now.
blocks.html: The yellow fever rules for Tanzania can be a little confusing at times, but we’re happy to help! Tanzania is a yellow fever-free country, so you are safe from this virus when you travel there. You might have further questions, so let’s go through them now.

blocks.orig: Yellow fever is a viral disease spread through mosquito bites. Symptoms of yellow fever typically take three to six days to develop and can include fever, chills, headache, and muscle aches. Yellow fever is serious: around 15% of people who get yellow fever develop a serious or life-threatening illness.
blocks.html: Yellow fever is a virus transmitted by mosquito bites. Symptoms usually appear after three to six days and may include fever, chills, headache and aching muscles. It is a serious disease: about 15% of those infected develop a severe or life-threatening illness.

blocks.orig: As Tanzania is safe from yellow fever, there are no yellow fever vaccine requirements if you are directly travelling from Europe or from the United States.
blocks.html: Because Tanzania is free from yellow fever, you don’t need a yellow fever vaccination when you travel there directly from Europe or the United States.

blocks.orig: Great news: for the vast majority of travellers to this beautiful country, you do not need this vaccine! According to the World Health Organization’s classification, Tanzania currently poses a low risk of yellow fever. If you reside in a country with no risk of yellow fever, then you don’t need the yellow fever vaccine as part of your necessary travel vaccinations.
blocks.html: Good news: the large majority of visitors to this beautiful country don’t need this vaccination! Under the World Health Organization’s classification, the risk of yellow fever in Tanzania is currently low. If you live in a country without yellow fever risk, the yellow fever vaccine is not one of the travel vaccinations you need.

blocks.orig: Proof of yellow fever vaccination is only required upon arrival if you come from a country with a risk of the virus. This list currently doesn’t include any country in Europe or in the United States. If you travel to Tanzania from a different country, check out the full list of yellow fever high-risk countries.
blocks.html: You only need to show proof of yellow fever vaccination on arrival if you travel from a country where the virus is a risk. At present, no country in Europe or the United States is on that list. Travelling to Tanzania from somewhere else? Then look at the complete list of high-risk yellow fever countries.

blocks.orig: An important note: if you’re transiting through one of the yellow fever high-risk countries for a period of twelve hours or more, you are required to receive the yellow fever vaccination. If this is the case on your trip to Tanzania, we strongly advise seeing your doctor and checking your Tanzania vaccination requirements with a healthcare professional before travelling.
blocks.html: Please note: if you transit through a yellow fever high-risk country for twelve hours or longer, the yellow fever vaccination is compulsory. If that applies to your journey to Tanzania, we strongly recommend visiting your doctor and confirming your Tanzania vaccination requirements with a health professional before you go.

blocks.orig: The yellow fever vaccination is given as a single dose and should be administered at least ten days before entering a high-risk yellow fever country. A single dose can provide life-protection against the yellow fever virus, so make sure you receive proof of vaccination from your doctor or health professional. If you are required to receive a yellow fever vaccine before travelling, you will also need to show your proof of vaccination upon arrival in Tanzania.
blocks.html: The yellow fever vaccine is a single dose that must be given at least ten days before you enter a high-risk yellow fever country. One dose can protect you for life against the virus, so be sure to get proof of vaccination from your doctor or health professional. If you need a yellow fever vaccination before your trip, you will also have to present that proof when you arrive in Tanzania.

blocks.orig: Should your doctor recommend against the vaccine due to underlying health issues or other health-related factors, you can still travel to Tanzania with an official letter from the doctor. Showing it to the immigration officer upon arrival would waive the requirement, and your trip can go on as planned.

For 40 USD per person, you can travel worry-free to any remote area in one or more of the following countries for 30 days: Tanzania, Kenya, Uganda, Burundi, and Rwanda.

blocks.orig: In a medical emergency, Flying Doctors can give professional advice or immediately evacuate you to a hospital in Nairobi, Kenya. blocks.orig: And if, by some freak accident, you badly break your leg while getting on a boat in Uganda’s Queen Elizabeth National Park, or a pre-existing medical condition suddenly causes trouble in the middle of Tanzania’s Serengeti National Park (knock on wood!), in no time a flight with a whole team of medical professionals can be waiting for you at the nearest airstrip. blocks.orig: First, avoid visiting the deep south of the country, right next to the Mozambican border, since there have been relatively high crime rates recorded there in recent years. Luckily, the tourist attractions aren’t anywhere near this region of Tanzania, so there should be no reason for you to visit the far south of Tanzania.
